evidence.claim: Thirteen paved miles beneath cliffs where older rock lies over younger rock
evidence.quote: Red Rock Canyon Back Country Byway spans for 13 miles across a paved loop

evidence.claim: cliffs where older rock lies over younger rock

evidence.claim: Red Rock Canyon Back Country Byway makes a 13-mile paved loop through red- and cream-colored sandstone country west of Las Vegas.
evidence.quote: Red Rock Canyon Back Country Byway spans for 13 miles across a paved loop through the Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area.

evidence.claim: red- and cream-colored sandstone country west of Las Vegas.
evidence.quote: Visit the red- and cream-colored sandstone cliffs and experience the natural wonders of the Mohave Desert just 17 miles west of the Las Vegas Strip.

evidence.claim: The one-way road starts with a moderate climb, then runs mostly downhill or flat, with side roads and parking areas serving trails.
evidence.quote: The loop road is also popular for bicycle touring; it begins with a moderate climb, then is mostly downhill or flat.

evidence.claim: The one-way road
evidence.quote: A one-way, loop road, 13 miles (21 km) long

evidence.claim: with side roads and parking areas serving trails.
evidence.quote: Several side roads and parking areas allow access to many of the area trails.

evidence.claim: BLM lists it as a Type I Back Country Byway, highlights the colors of its rock formations and suggests allowing an hour.
evidence.quote: Red Rock Canyon Back Country Byway - Type I

evidence.claim: highlights the colors of its rock formations
evidence.quote: enjoy the spectacular colors in the rock formations.

evidence.claim: suggests allowing an hour.
evidence.quote: This byway is 13 miles long, allow 1 hour to enjoy it.

evidence.claim: Sandstone walls rise as much as 3,000 feet.
evidence.quote: The walls are up to 3,000 feet (910 m) high

evidence.claim: Near the loop's northern section, the Excelsior Company quarried sandstone in the early 20th century.
evidence.quote: In the early 20th century, around the time the first European Americans settled in nearby Las Vegas, the Excelsior Company operated a small sandstone quarry near the northern area of the scenic loop.

evidence.claim: The business proved uneconomical and closed, leaving huge sandstone blocks behind.
evidence.quote: It proved to be uneconomical and was shut down. Evidence of the quarry's existence includes some of the huge sandstone blocks that have been left behind.

evidence.claim: Protection followed: BLM designated 10,000 acres as Red Rock Recreation Lands in 1967, and legislation changed their status to a National Conservation Area in 1990.
evidence.quote: In 1967, the Bureau of Land Management designated 10,000 acres (16 sq mi; 40 km2) as the Red Rock Recreation Lands.

evidence.claim: legislation changed their status to a National Conservation Area in 1990.
evidence.quote: Further legislation in 1990 changed the status of the Red Rock Recreation Lands to a National Conservation Area

evidence.claim: The new conservation status also provides funds to maintain and protect the area that the scenic loop travels through.
evidence.quote: Further legislation in 1990 changed the status of the Red Rock Recreation Lands to a National Conservation Area, a status that also provides funds to maintain and protect it.

evidence.claim: Begin at the visitor center, which stands at the start of the loop.
evidence.quote: A visitor center is at the start of the loop road.

evidence.claim: The northern quarry preserves evidence of stonecutting; Willow Springs provides an approach on foot to Bridge Mountain, a separate mountain excursion.
evidence.quote: Hikers can park at the north Willow Springs campground and walk 5 miles (8 km) to the summit.

evidence.claim: The northern quarry preserves evidence of stonecutting
evidence.quote: Evidence of the quarry's existence includes some of the huge sandstone blocks that have been left behind.

evidence.claim: Along the escarpment, the Keystone Thrust exposes older gray rock pushed over younger red rock.
evidence.quote: The movement of this fault forced the older gray sedimentary rock over the younger red rocks

evidence.claim: Its exposed seam extends for 13 miles along the cliffs.
evidence.quote: The thrust is exposed over a distance of 13 miles (21 km) along the Red Rock escarpment.

evidence.claim: The visitor center marks the start of the one-way scenic loop.
evidence.quote: A visitor center is at the start of the loop road.

evidence.claim: A desert tortoise habitat here connects the road's starting point with one of the conservation area's protected animals.
evidence.quote: The Conservation Area is a protected habitat for the desert tortoise. A habitat at the Visitor Center houses eight females and two males.

evidence.claim: The surrounding vegetation changes with elevation: Joshua trees, Mojave yucca and blackbrush grow on the valley floor, while Utah juniper and scrub oak dominate higher ground.
evidence.quote: Common types in the valley floor include the Joshua tree, Mojave yucca, banana yucca, creosote, and blackbrush. Higher up the Utah juniper and Sonoran scrub oak (also called scrub live oak) come to dominate.

evidence.claim: The conservation area spans two elevation zones, with the Upper Sonoran Zone beginning at 4,500 feet and extending into higher country.
evidence.quote: the area from 4,500 feet (1,400 m) up is in the Upper Sonoran Zone.

evidence.claim: two elevation zones
evidence.quote: the lowest elevation of the area, from 3,600 to 4,500 feet (1,100 to 1,400 m), is in the Lower Sonoran Zone, while the area from 4,500 feet (1,400 m) up is in the Upper Sonoran Zone.

evidence.claim: From the center, the loop climbs moderately before continuing through its mostly downhill or level sections.
evidence.quote: it begins with a moderate climb, then is mostly downhill or flat.

evidence.claim: Timed-entry reservations are required for each day of scenic-drive entry from October 1 through May 31, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
evidence.quote: Visitors must have a timed entry reservation for each day they plan to enter, October 1 to May 31, 8am -5pm.

evidence.claim: Huge sandstone blocks remain where the Excelsior Company operated a small quarry near the northern part of the loop.
evidence.quote: Evidence of the quarry's existence includes some of the huge sandstone blocks that have been left behind.

evidence.claim: The company worked here in the early 20th century, then closed the quarry when it proved uneconomical.
evidence.quote: In the early 20th century, around the time the first European Americans settled in nearby Las Vegas, the Excelsior Company operated a small sandstone quarry near the northern area of the scenic loop. It proved to be uneconomical and was shut down.

evidence.claim: The stone has a much longer history: immense dunes became cemented into the colorful Aztec Sandstone.
evidence.quote: These dunes accumulated over a broad area, up to 0.5 miles (0.80 km) thick, and were lithified, cemented with calcium carbonate and iron oxides. They developed as the colorful Aztec Sandstone.

evidence.claim: Sandstone Quarry is also a rock-climbing area.
evidence.quote: Popular sport climbing areas include the Calico Hills and Sandstone Quarry.

evidence.claim: Look for the huge sandstone blocks left by the abandoned quarry.
evidence.quote: Evidence of the quarry's existence includes some of the huge sandstone blocks that have been left behind.

evidence.claim: Bridge Mountain takes its name from a sandstone arch near the summit.
evidence.quote: Bridge Mountain is named for the natural feature of a bridge-like natural arch of sandstone near the summit.

evidence.claim: The arch is the remaining side of an eroded tinaja, a natural water tank.
evidence.quote: The bridge itself is the remains of a tinaja, or water tank, that eroded and left a remnant of the side, now a bridge.

evidence.claim: Reaching this terrain involves steep climbing down a chimney, an ascent over slickrock and a difficult ridge near the top.
evidence.quote: Here, steep free climbing down a chimney

evidence.claim: an ascent over slickrock
evidence.quote: The hike ascends the slickrock here

evidence.claim: a difficult ridge near the top.
evidence.quote: one then must climb along a steep, difficult ridge to get near the top.

evidence.claim: From north Willow Springs, the approach to the summit is five miles.
evidence.quote: Hikers can park at the north Willow Springs campground and walk 5 miles (8 km) to the summit.

evidence.claim: The route crosses a narrow rock neck between the Pine Creek drainage to the south and Icebox Canyon to the north.
evidence.quote: a narrow neck of rock that separates the drainages of Pine Creek to the south and Icebox Canyon to the north.

evidence.claim: The mountain belongs to the Spring Mountain range and lies within the Rainbow Mountain Wilderness.
evidence.quote: Bridge Mountain is a mountain located in the Spring Mountain range of southern Nevada. It is located on land managed by the United States Bureau of Land Management as the Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area, part of the Rainbow Mountain Wilderness.

evidence.claim: Ponderosa pines grow in a cleft in the summit sandstone.
evidence.quote: In a cleft in the sandstone of Bridge Mountain's summit, there is a small hidden forest of Ponderosa pine.

flags: Cache supports driving character and conservation history but gives no loop builder, construction date or designation campaign. Overview uses quarry-to-conservation history without inventing a causal link.
Retained visitor center and Bridge Mountain titles and all existing coordinates/motifs. Added Sandstone Quarry without coordinates because no dedicated Wikipedia cache page supplies its coordinates.

Order is visitor center, northern quarry, Willow Springs mountain excursion. Material places the mountain by summit projection at mile 3.07, not its trail access; no precise access mileage claimed. Cache does not provide a complete ordered loop map.

Current “mix of colors is the work of the Keystone Thrust” revised: thrusting juxtaposed old and young rocks; sandstone color also involves iron minerals. No other current factual claim lacks cache support.

Tortoise sex/count detail is in the cache but omitted as changeable and supported only by a secondary source. Habitat retained without promising a sighting. Current warmer-month recommendation omitted as unnecessary seasonal advice.

NCA history interleaves a 1973 hearing with approval by President George H. W. Bush; that legislative narrative is chronologically inconsistent and omitted. Disagreement over highest summit (La Madre versus Mount Wilson in separate pages) is irrelevant and omitted.
Bridge Mountain is a climbing excursion, not an easy five-mile walk; no turn-by-turn climbing instructions or drive to the primitive trailhead are offered.
Sandstone Quarry moment is short because the cache provides only a brief quarry history. Reservation checked date means review of the saved BLM page, not a live access check.
